title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; 1/7 of week lost. Historical data shows no direct closure effect, but a 14% sales loss is plausible given no other drivers. Adjusted for noise and uncertainty.

drivers.name: Price increase (+5.5%)
drivers.evidence: Recent weeks at $10.81 show median 35.0 vs baseline 35.1 (x0.997). Noise-adjusted price effect is modestly negative. Not strong enough to override closure.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 35.1. No events are scheduled. The store closes Monday, reducing the selling week by 1 day. Price is up 5.5% vs regular, which historically reduces demand. Recent weeks at $10.81 show lower sales (avg 35.0 vs baseline 35.1), suggesting a small negative price effect. No promotion or holiday is planned. The uplift model suggests no change, but planner notes indicate a store closure. The closure reduces potential sales by ~14%, but the baseline already accounts for some irregularity. Adjust downward with caution due to thin evidence. Noise-adjusted price effect is negative, but weak. Final multiplier shrinks toward 1.0.

brief:
PRODUCT: AA Batteries 8-pack | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.81 (+5.5% vs regular price 10.25)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 35.1 | 5%-95%: 19.6 - 57.2 | 10%-90%: 21.8 - 54.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
